title: Ambush at the felled oak
text: Escorting Bram the tinker toward Imre, Sebak spots a felled oak across the road. A crossbowman waits in an ash tree and two brigands crouch in the hawthorn ditch. Sebak acts first in the surprise round.

title: The crow in the wind
text: At the felled oak Sebak dropped the crossbowman from behind, killed one brigand and fell to the other's club. As the final blow came down, something in his blood answered: every scrap of iron and wood nearby rang like a struck bell, the brigand's club burst apart in his hands, and he fled screaming into the hawthorn. Sebak woke at 1 HP, empty of chakra and shaking, with Bram bleeding beside him and the crossbowman still senseless in the ash tree.

title: A roof in Imre
text: Sebak drove Bram through the night to Imre and found an apothecary awake before dawn. He paid a talent for Bram's treatment, got a loft and a stall for the mule, and slept until midday, rested and whole.

title: A report at the south gate
text: On the apothecary's advice, Sebak reported the ambush to Sergeant Haldric Voss at the south gate. He told it plainly: the crossbowman in the ash, the two brigands, one dead, one fled, and Bram wounded. Voss held the looted crossbow for a month on a receipt and is sending men for the bodies. Sebak recalled that the crossbowman waited patiently, aimed at Bram and not at him, and carried a small iron key, which Sebak kept. Voss thinks the man was hired. Sebak will be at the apothecary's or the wharf.

title: A visitor in the loft
text: In the small hours the twine alarm tugged Sebak awake to find a masked intruder at Bram's strongbox. Sebak slammed the hatch, failed to sweep the intruder's legs and took a short blade across the ribs, then flickered behind him and wounded him, burned him through the blood on his own blade with the lantern's flame, and knocked him senseless with the pommel. Marta woke below and called up. The intruder lies unconscious and unmasked-not-yet in the loft.

title: The burglar, the box and the counting house
text: Sebak bound the intruder, questioned him, and learned he was a hired burglar named Pell. Sergeant Voss took Pell and sent men to the Salt Barrel. Sebak questioned Bram about the strongbox, and later secured it, the iron key and the six pale bars in a counting house on Lamplight Street under the name Crow, replacing the bars in the box with stones.

title: A man in grey
text: At the Artificery loading dock Sebak met a thin man in a long grey coat who called himself Ashdown, who claimed the bars were his and offered a bar and an hour of teaching for them. Rennick had named the buyer as Warrick, a journeywoman of the Artificery. Sebak scouted Penn's chandler on Candle Row, the grey man's post-drop, and caught the boy who watched it.

title: The Fishery gate
text: Sebak gave Warrick one bar at the Stonebridge gardens and followed the other five to the Artificery, where Master Orrel took them in by a postern. Warrick checked her master's cabinet and found the bars. Sebak was held in the yard, flickered out, and the watch sent everyone to the wardens. Warden Isk found the five bars in Orrel's cold furnace and confiscated them. Orrel is suspended and the porter Dobb has fled.

title: Dobb in the cellar
text: Penn confessed that Dobb was hiding in his cellar. Dobb admitted he sold Penn's post to Orrel, copied Ashdown's key, and hid the bars in the furnace on Orrel's orders. Orrel hired the robbers through the crossbowman Verrin, who is still loose. Dobb will testify to the wardens at first bell. Sebak intends to join the Academy.

title: The wardens' hall
text: At first bell Sebak, Ashdown and the porter Dobb crossed the river to the wardens' hall. Dobb told Warden Isk everything: the stolen routes, the furnace and the men Orrel hired. Isk took him into protective custody, summoned Orrel and sent wardens after Verrin and his fellows. She heard Sebak's account and offered a sealed letter of character for the University.

title: The road to the University
text: After the wardens' hall Sebak said goodbye to Bram and Marta and left Imre with Warden Isk's sealed letter. On the river path he met Tamsin, a fellow applicant, taught him a better heat binding and rebound his mule's leg. They stopped at the Ferry-Pole inn, where a University ledger-keeper named Hale explained the interview and a drover told of three grey-cloaked robbers on the east road.

title: Ambush on the ridge road
text: Following Hale's map, Sebak walked straight into the ambush he expected on the ridge road. A hooded man clubbed Tamsin down, but Sebak flickered behind the limping leader Marsh and cut him down with a critical wakizashi strike, then threw a kunai around the boulders and dropped the crossbowman Finch. The hooded man fled, and Sebak stabilised the dying Tamsin.
